SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient: Reese Template, 50-year-old female.
HPI: She reports onset of low back pain on 06/16/2026. She describes aching low back pain worsened by extension and relieved by flexion. She denies trauma, fever, weight loss, or bowel/bladder symptoms.
Exam: Tenderness over lumbar paraspinals, limited range of motion. Straight leg raise negative. Neurologic exam shows diminished ankle reflex on the left; strength 5/5 elsewhere, sensation intact.
Assessment: Acute lumbar musculoligamentous strain with possible L5/S1 radiculopathy.
Plan: Initiate ibuprofen 600 mg PO q6h PRN starting today (06/17/2026). Prescribe home exercises. Order physical therapy evaluation to start in the coming days. Follow up in 2 weeks.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient: Reese Template, 50-year-old female.
HPI: She returns for follow‑up of low back pain. She reports ongoing discomfort but notes some relief with NSAIDs. She denies any red-flag symptoms such as trauma, cancer history, fever, weight loss, bowel or bladder dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficit.
Exam: Lumbar spine tender to palpation, mild paraspinal spasm. Straight leg raise negative. Neurologic examination reveals diminished ankle reflex and L5/S1-myotome weakness consistent with L5/S1 radiculopathy. Strength 4/5 in left extensor hallucis longus, otherwise 5/5.
Assessment: Persistent lumbar radiculopathy, L5/S1 level, inadequate response to conservative measures.
Plan: Continue NSAID as needed. Complete the remaining physical therapy sessions today (final session). After today’s session, the prescribed course of 10 PT visits will be finished. Obtain lumbar MRI to further evaluate disc pathology; pending results, consider spine surgery referral.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient: Reese Template, 50-year-old female.
HPI: She reports persistent low back pain with radicular symptoms. She reports onset of low back pain on 06/16/2026.
Exam: Tenderness lumbar spine, limited forward flexion. Straight leg raise negative. Neurologic exam shows diminished ankle reflex and L5/S1 weakness; otherwise normal.
Assessment: Chronic lumbar radiculopathy, L5/S1, failing conservative therapy.
Plan: NSAID therapy was started on 06/17/2026 and continued through 07/26/2026 with partial response. She underwent a course of physical therapy from 06/21/2026 to 07/26/2026 consisting of 10 sessions, which yielded no improvement. Pending the lumbar MRI results, a referral for spine surgery consultation will be considered. Obtain lumbar MRI today.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient: Reese Template, 50-year-old female.
HPI: She returns for follow‑up after completing conservative therapy. She reports ongoing low back pain with radiculopathy.
Exam: Similar to prior: tenderness lumbar spine, diminished ankle reflex and L5/S1 weakness.
Assessment: Lumbar radiculopathy, L5/S1, unresponsive to NSAIDs and physical therapy.
Plan: Order lumbar spine MRI today (07/31/2026). Pending results, consider spine surgery referral.
